description: Add Prime Intellect's prime-agent as a first-class Open Harness harness with its own provider surface: .prime/agent/skills symlinked into the vendored .oh/skills pack, a minimal provider-neutral .prime/agent/ config surface, an on-demand harness catalog entry, docs, and parity-probe coverage. No image-level install in this pass.

userStories.title: Wire .prime/agent/skills in link-providers.sh
userStories.description: As an operator with a running Open Harness checkout, I want `bash .oh/scripts/link-providers.sh --init` to create and `--check` to verify the prime-agent skill surface, so that the harness loads every Open Harness skill on its first launch.
acceptanceCriteria: `.oh/scripts/link-providers.sh`'s `provider_links` array carries the row `.prime/agent/skills|../../.oh/skills`.
The row uses no Hermes-style special case; `link_provider()`'s existing `mkdir -p` on the link's parent creates the intermediate `.prime/agent` directory.
`bash .oh/scripts/link-providers.sh --init` creates `.prime/agent/skills` as a symlink to `../../.oh/skills`.
`bash .oh/scripts/link-providers.sh --check` passes with the new row present and fails when the link is missing or mistargeted.
`.prime/agent/skills/git/SKILL.md` resolves to the vendored pack file.
`print_state()`'s `Provider surfaces:` line names the prime surface alongside the others.
The final success line names the prime surface alongside the others.
`bash -n .oh/scripts/link-providers.sh` reports no syntax error and shellcheck at `-S warning` reports no new finding.

userStories.title: Wire the same link in the oh init scaffolder
userStories.description: As someone running `oh init` in a fresh project, I want the prime surface scaffolded alongside the other four, so that the two independent wiring mechanisms do not drift.
acceptanceCriteria: `.oh/cli/src/commands/init.ts`'s `PROVIDER_LINKS` carries the `.prime/agent/skills` entry targeting `../../.oh/skills`.
The provider-surface summary line counts five surfaces and names `.prime` among them.
`npm --prefix .oh/cli test` passes.
The repo's typecheck/build for `.oh/cli` reports no error.
userStories.notes: init.ts keeps its own copy of the link list; the two lists are the drift risk this story closes.

userStories.title: Ship the .prime/agent/ config surface, live and as a template
userStories.description: As an operator, I want a minimal committed prime config surface in the repo and in the `oh init` template, so that a fresh launch has the project context loaded and no per-machine setup.
acceptanceCriteria: `.prime/agent/settings.json` exists at repo root and is tracked.

`settings.json` sets only provider-neutral keys (theme, thinking level, steering/follow-up mode) and carries no model pin, no provider name, and no npm package list — none of Pi's `.pi/settings.json` values are copied.
`settings.json` declares no `skills` array, because `.prime/agent/skills/` discovery is automatic.
Parsing `.prime/agent/settings.json` as JSON succeeds.
`.prime/agent/APPEND_SYSTEM.md` exists and points the agent at `AGENTS.md` and the vendored skill pack; it carries no Slack-bridge and no Pi-extension content.
`.prime/agent/.gitignore` ignores `sessions/` and `telemetry.json`.
`.oh/templates/full/.prime/agent/` carries the same three files, so `collectRealFiles()` copies them with no code change.
The live and template copies of each file are byte-identical.
userStories.notes: prime-agent is its own harness; do not model its config on Pi's.

userStories.title: Ignore prime runtime state
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want prime-agent session and telemetry state kept out of git, so that running the harness never dirties the tree.
acceptanceCriteria: `.gitignore` ignores `.prime/agent/sessions/` and `.prime/agent/telemetry.json`.
`.oh/templates/gitignore` carries the same rules.
Credentials remain covered by the existing `**/auth.json` rule; no duplicate rule is added for it.
`git check-ignore -v` reports both prime runtime paths as ignored.
`git status --short` is clean after a `link-providers.sh --init` run.

userStories.title: Add the on-demand harness catalog entry
userStories.description: As an operator, I want `oh harness install prime-agent` to install the CLI into the already-running sandbox, so that trying the harness costs no image rebuild.
acceptanceCriteria: `.oh/cli/src/lib/harnesses/catalog.ts` carries an entry with id `prime-agent`, binary `prime-agent`, and kind `on-demand`.
The entry declares no `harnessKey` and no `buildArg`, so `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`, `.devcontainer/docker-compose.yml`, and both `.example.env` files stay untouched.
`installArgv` is exactly three elements: `bash`, `-lc`, and a fixed literal shell string containing no shell interpolation.
The installer runs non-interactively — verified in-sandbox — or the argv is adjusted until it does.
`installUser` is `sandbox`, matching pi and deepagents, so `prime-agent update` needs no sudo.
`verifyArgv` invokes the installed binary's version flag.
`docsPath` is `.oh/docs/harnesses/prime-agent.md` and that file exists.
`npm --prefix .oh/cli test` passes, including every assertion in `harness-catalog.test.ts`.
`.oh/evals/probes/env-schema-parity.sh` still passes.
userStories.notes: t3code is the on-demand precedent to copy.

userStories.title: Own ~/.prime in the container entrypoint
userStories.description: As an operator installing the harness on demand, I want the prime global config directory writable by the sandbox user, so that login does not fail on permissions.
acceptanceCriteria: `.devcontainer/entrypoint.sh`'s chown list includes `.prime`.
`.prime` is the only change made to `.devcontainer/` in this pass.
`bash -n .devcontainer/entrypoint.sh` reports no syntax error.

userStories.title: Document the harness
userStories.description: As a reader, I want prime-agent named wherever the other harnesses are named, so that the surface is discoverable without reading the catalog source.
acceptanceCriteria: `.oh/docs/harnesses/prime-agent.md` exists, carries the same frontmatter shape as its siblings, and documents install, authentication, config paths, how the Open Harness skills reach the agent, and the headless flags.
`.oh/docs/harnesses/overview.md` names prime-agent in the intro prose, the Supported agents table, the verify block, and the Authentication list.
`AGENTS.md`'s sentence naming which providers expose `.oh/skills` through symlinks includes prime.
`README.md`'s provider-symlink description includes prime.
`.oh/context/REPO_MAP.md` routes `.prime/` alongside `.pi/`, `.claude/`, and `.hermes/`.

`.oh/skills/wiki/corpus/prime-agent-harness.md` exists, cites source files with line numbers for each structural claim, states the two wiring mechanisms and the on-demand classification, and carries a `## See Also`.
`bash .oh/evals/probes/wiki-readme-index.sh` passes after the index refresh.
No doc claims an image-level install, a Dockerfile flag, or messenger-bridge support exists.
userStories.notes: docsPath in the catalog makes prime-agent.md a hard test dependency.

userStories.title: Extend the parity probe
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the existing vendored-skills oracle to cover the prime surface, so that a future refactor that drops the link fails a command instead of passing review.
acceptanceCriteria: `.oh/evals/probes/skills-vendored.sh`'s resolve loop includes `.prime/agent/skills`.
The clean-clone section asserts `.prime/agent/skills/git/SKILL.md` exists after `--init`.
No new probe file is added; the existing oracle is extended.
`bash .oh/evals/probes/skills-vendored.sh` exits 0.
The probe fails when the prime row is removed from `provider_links` — verified by a temporary removal, then restored.
